reason: E2 directly supports the mechanism of heterogeneous microstructures generating GNDs and back-stress strengthening in a hybrid-rolled EHEA, but it does not address cryogenic rolling, modulus enhancement, or fracture resistance. E1 and E3 discuss general strategies for strength-ductility improvement and heterogeneous design, but neither provides specific evidence for the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 system, the cryo/warm rolling route, or the claimed improvements in Young’s modulus and fracture resistance. Thus, the core mechanism is partly supported, but several key premises lack direct cited evidence.
premises: Hybrid cryo/warm rolling of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA can produce a heterogeneous nanostructure with retained deformed and partially recrystallized zones.
Such heterogeneous microstructures generate strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations (GNDs) that produce long-range back stress.
Long-range back stress retards necking, promotes uniform plastic flow, and simultaneously enhances strength, ductility, modulus, and fracture resistance.
The proposed processing (cryo-rolling + warm rolling + 800°C anneal) will yield ~15–20% higher yield strength, ~15% higher ductility, and enhanced fracture resistance vs. a cold-rolled baseline.
